definitions.gloss: to get to the heart of the matter; to hit the nail on the head
definitions.explanation: To identify or address the most important, central point of an issue. Used when someone makes a remark or asks a question that goes straight to the core of a problem.

examples.japanese: {核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く{質問|しつもん}だった。
examples.english: It was a question that hit the nail on the head.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{発言|はつげん}は{問題|もんだい}の{核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}いていた。
examples.english: Her remark got to the heart of the problem.

examples.japanese: {記者|きしゃ}が{核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く{質問|しつもん}をしたが、{大臣|だいじん}は{明確|めいかく}な{回答|かいとう}を{避|さ}けた。
examples.english: The reporter asked a pointed question that went to the heart of the matter, but the minister avoided giving a clear answer.

notes:
USAGE:
{核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く is used when someone identifies the central, most important point of an issue. It is often used to describe incisive questions, remarks, or analyses. The verb {突|つ}く conjugates as godan: {突|つ}く → {突|つ}いた → {突|つ}いて.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く{質問|しつもん} (a question that gets to the heart of the matter)
- {核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く{発言|はつげん} (a remark that hits the mark)
- {核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}いた{指摘|してき} (an observation that identifies the core issue)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {的|まと}を{射|い}る (to hit the mark — similar but broader)
- {痛|いた}いところを{突|つ}く (to touch a sore spot — more personal/uncomfortable)
